# Section 040: Cost Visibility With OpenCost

The reader makes cost visible: OpenCost splits node, storage and network cost across namespaces, workloads and labels, and shows idle capacity. It follows autoscaling because the reader can now act on what the cost report shows.

**Curriculum item covered:** Using Cost Management Solutions for Right-Sizing and Scaling

---

## What You Will Master

- Name the data OpenCost needs (Prometheus metrics, node prices) and where each comes from on a cluster without cloud billing
- Query cost allocation by namespace and by controller with the OpenCost API and the kubectl cost style output
- Read the CPU, memory and storage parts of a workload's cost and the efficiency figure
- Explain how OpenCost allocates cost from the larger of requests and usage
- Aggregate cost by a team label and by namespace in the OpenCost API
- Find workloads with low cost efficiency and name the requests to change
- Read idle cost and explain how it shrinks when requests fit the nodes better
- Add cost-attribution labels to workloads and confirm OpenCost picks them up

---

## The Learning Path

### 1. Read Cost Allocation With OpenCost
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Read Cost Allocation With OpenCost](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-01/playground` — Single-node kind cluster with metrics-server, a small Prometheus (prometheus-community/prometheus chart) and OpenCost 1.121.3 with its default on-premises price list. Namespaces `starfleet` (`scout`, `probe`, `shuttle` with load) and `outpost` (`probe`), running long enough before the reader arrives for allocation data to be non-zero. The OpenCost UI is reachable through kubectl port-forward.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-040/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Attribute Cost By Label And Find Idle Spend
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Attribute Cost By Label And Find Idle Spend](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-02/playground` — Same base as the OpenCost reading module: kind, metrics-server, Prometheus, OpenCost with the default price list. `starfleet` workloads carry a `team` label; one `outpost` Deployment has no `team` label (the deliberate gap), and `scout-overprovisioned` requests far more than it uses, so low efficiency and idle cost are visible.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-040/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Cost Visibility Capstone — `sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS017.git -c sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** The finance team needs the cost of each team. The reader labels every workload with its team, reports cost per team for the last hour from the OpenCost API, finds the least efficient workload and right-sizes its requests, and shows the efficiency change.
